agent.problem: Nothing in the opening card distinguishes who will see Zion's righteousness. Choosing "nations" over "priests" or "prophets" requires already knowing verse 2, so the blank tests an unseen detail rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The only treatment of the second half of verse 11 is the false statement that the Savior comes empty-handed. No card tells the baker that His reward is with Him and His recompense goes before Him, leaving an important part of the proclamation untaught.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: The closing question elicits only "Sought Out," and no card mentions the verse's other name, "A City Not Forsaken." The walkthrough ends without teaching the full closing promise and its bookend to Zion's old name.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

human.problem: In 62:1 the speaker of 'I will not keep silent' is not identified. It could be the prophet or the LORD. The card calls it 'a voice'. papa-dorin.md says that when he quotes someone speaking as 'I', he says who it is first. The Scripture rules also say to leave open what the text leaves open.
human.question: When a passage's 'I' speaker is ambiguous (prophet or the LORD), should Papa Dorin name a speaker before quoting, or is an unnamed 'voice' the right way to follow 'leave open what the text leaves open'?

human.problem: The joke makes up a moment in the Millers' kitchen: 'I'd turn around and half a batch was GONE off the cooling rack'. papa-dorin.md lets jokes make up small moments around his bakery but says he never adds anything new to his backstory. The Millers' kitchen is backstory, not his bakery. The joke also casts the Millers' family in the role of the enemies and foreigners of 62:8.
human.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes make up small moments set in the Millers' kitchen, or only in his Dorinverse bakery?

human.problem: Card 1 quotes a speaker using 'I' ('I will not keep silent… I will not keep still') and calls it only 'a voice'. Isaiah 62:1 does not say whether the speaker is the LORD or the prophet. Two rules point different ways. papa-dorin.md says that when he quotes an 'I' speaker 'he says who it is first'. The Scripture rules say to leave open what the text leaves open. The opening card is also meant to say who is speaking.
human.question: When a passage quotes an 'I' speaker the text doesn't identify, as in Isaiah 62:1 and 62:6, should Papa Dorin leave the speaker unnamed ('a voice')? Or should he name the most likely speaker, or say the speaker isn't named?
